title: God Pictured as a Caring Shepherd
overview: A short poem of trust that pictures God first as a shepherd caring for a sheep, then as a generous host welcoming a guest.

parts.label: The shepherd who provides (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: The speaker pictures the LORD as a shepherd and himself as a sheep that lacks nothing, with fresh grass to rest in and calm water to drink. Christians later read this in light of Jesus, who called himself the good shepherd.

parts.label: Revived and guided (v. 3)
parts.note: The shepherd brings the sheep back to life and strength, and leads it along safe, good paths that God approves of. He does this "for his name's sake," meaning because it fits who he is and what he has promised, not because the sheep has earned it.

parts.label: Through the darkest valley (v. 4)
parts.note: The image is a deep, shadowy ravine where wild animals could hide, and translations render it either as deep darkness or as the shadow of death, so it can cover any great danger, including dying. Here the speaker turns to speak to God directly, and the shepherd's rod (a club against attackers) and staff (a stick for guiding) reassure him.

parts.label: A guest at God's table (v. 5)
parts.note: The picture shifts to a host who sets out a meal, pours oil on the guest's head as a sign of honor and gladness, and fills the cup past the brim. The guest feasts in full view of his enemies, a picture of being cared for even while opposition is still around.

parts.label: At home with God (v. 6)
parts.note: The word for "follow" can mean pursue, as if God's goodness and loyal love chase after the speaker. "The house of the LORD" likely meant the place of worship, and the closing phrase is literally "for length of days," so scholars are unsure whether it first meant a whole lifetime or something beyond death.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether the closing hope of dwelling in the LORD's house originally pointed to life after death or to a lifelong closeness with God in worship, though many read it as both.
think: When life has felt like a dark valley, what, if anything, made you feel less alone in it?
